title: Canva’s backers cut $7.1bn from its valuation, and its own valuer cut more
excerpt: Blackbird and Airtree cut the Canva valuation to $34.9bn, and Canva's internal mark fell further, after AI costs forced a revenue downgrade.
content_html:
Emma Rapaport and Paul Smith reported the markdown for the Australian Financial Review on 14 August.

The figure appears two ways and both are correct. It is $7.1bn in US dollars, and A$10bn, which is the number most headlines carried.

The cut takes Blackbird and Airtree’s mark from $42bn to $34.9bn, a drop of 17%. Both firms are among Canva’s longest-standing backers.

The bigger cut came from inside

Canva’s own independent valuation has moved further than its investors’ did. The AFR notes that the internal downgrade surpasses theirs.

That number matters because it is not an opinion. It is the price employees can sell shares at, and it has gone from $38.9bn to $31bn over the past year.

So the write-down is $7.1bn on one measure and $7.9bn on the other. Two separate valuers, moving the same way.

Neither is a transaction. Nobody bought or sold Canva at these prices, and that distinction matters for what follows.

The downgrade that started it

The markdown came a week after the revenue news. The AFR reported on 3 August that Canva had cut its expected growth rate by a third, to 20%.

Its headline for that story named the cause directly. Canva had an AI bill shock.

The company found it difficult to roll out AI tools given the soaring cost of using frontier models. Second-quarter revenue reached $921.9m, up 25.2%, and missed its internal guidance.

Melanie Perkins says demand was the problem rather than the absence of it. Appetite for the new AI features “significantly exceeded” expectations.

Perkins on the decision to slow down

Her account to Fortune, by email, is the clearest statement of what happened. It is also unusually candid about sequencing.

The launch “validated the demand, but also showed us we needed to reduce the cost of completing an AI task to support a broad rollout”, she said.

Then the decision. “Rather than broadly rolling out a product before the underlying economics were ready, we decided to slow the rollout while we rebuilt the architecture, reduced unit costs and strengthened the business model.”

Cost per task has since fallen by nearly 90% since Canva AI 2.0 launched in April, she says. Users are creating three times as many designs, so the saving does not land where the percentage suggests.

What actually broke

Derek Hernandez, a senior research analyst at Pitchbook covering SaaS and AI, gave Fortune the structural version. Software’s economics are the casualty.

“AI is making SaaS no longer a zero marginal cost solution, which has really been what I would call a lot of software’s secret sauce up until now,” he said.

His analogy is the useful part. Building a Ford F-150 is training, and the petrol and the mechanic are inference, “because that’s the point of using the product”.

Serving one more user of a design tool used to cost almost nothing. Every AI-assisted image now arrives with a compute bill attached.

Five days apart

Hernandez also supplied the line connecting this to the listed markets. “Canva and Figma both hit the same wall about five days apart, but they cited it in different places,” he said.

Figma grew 48% and raised its outlook, and its stock fell 16% on margins.

Its free cash flow margin fell to 14% in the second quarter from 27% in the first. It has guided third-quarter growth to 36%, down from 48%.

One company is public and got repriced in a day. The other is private and got repriced by its shareholders. Same wall.

The same bill is arriving elsewhere

Large buyers are hitting it too. Amazon ran a Claude job that went 860% over budget before failing.

The responses are converging. Microsoft has put spending limits on internal AI use.

EY built an AI router to send tasks to cheaper models rather than defaulting to the frontier. That is close to what Perkins describes rebuilding.

Rory O’Driscoll of Scale Venture Partners put the timing argument on the 20VC podcast. “There’s going to be a lot of people paying the bill in 26 and 27 for a certain amount of hesitancy in 23 and 24,” he said.

Why Canva could not sit it out

AI is not a feature here, it is the expansion plan. Canva has been pushing beyond design into enterprise workflows, adding tools including Canva Code.

Perkins told Fortune in 2023 that the AI market was too fragmented. The strategy since has been to bring those pieces inside one platform.

That is the dilemma Fortune sets out for the whole sector. Companies cannot afford to skip the AI boom, and embracing it can undermine the economics they are protecting.

Europe has an entrant on the same premise, and no comparable margin history yet. Lovable reached $500m of revenue with 146 employees.

The listing is the reason for the brakes

Canva was valued at $42bn in an employee share sale, and expected to list in 2026. Hernandez now suggests next year.

He reads the slowdown as investor-facing. “I’m sure they’re trying to protect their profitability, especially if they want to go to public investors,” he said.

Growth of 20% with repaired margins is a different pitch to growth of 30% with a cost problem. Figma suggests public markets punish the second one immediately.

What would settle it

Three things, and the first is the next revenue print. Canva has guided to about 20%, and whether that holds shows if the cost problem is fixed or deferred.

The second is the 90% claim. A cost per task falling that far while usage triples is testable over a couple of quarters.

The third is who else gets marked down for this reason. Hernandez calls Canva and Figma the biggest signals so far, which implies more are coming.

content_html_zh:
艾玛·拉帕波特 (Emma Rapaport) 和保罗·史密斯 (Paul Smith) 于 8 月 14 日报道了《澳大利亚金融评论》的降价情况。

该图有两种显示方式，并且都是正确的。 换算为 71 亿美元和 100 亿澳元，这是头条新闻最多的数字。

此次削减使 Blackbird 和 Airtree 的营收从 420 亿美元降至 349 亿美元，下降了 17%。 两家公司都是 Canva 历史最悠久的支持者之一。

更大的切口来自内部

Canva 自身的独立估值比其投资者的估值更高。 AFR 指出，内部降级幅度超过了他们的降级幅度。

这个数字很重要，因为它不是意见。 这是员工出售股票的价格，在过去的一年里已经从 389 亿美元增至 310 亿美元。

因此，一项措施的减记额为 71 亿美元，另一项措施的减记额为 79 亿美元。 两个独立的评估师，以相同的方式移动。

两者都不是交易。 没有人以这些价格购买或出售 Canva，这种区别对于接下来的内容很重要。

开始的降级

降价是在收入消息公布一周后进行的。 AFR 8 月 3 日报道称，Canva 已将预期增长率下调三分之一，至 20%。

该报道的标题直接指出了原因。 Canva 对人工智能账单感到震惊。

该公司发现，鉴于使用前沿模型的成本不断飙升，推出人工智能工具非常困难。 第二季度收入达到 9.219 亿美元，增长 25.2%，未达到内部指引。

梅兰妮·珀金斯表示，需求才是问题所在，而不是缺乏需求。 对新人工智能功能的需求“大大超出”预期。

帕金斯决定放慢速度

她通过电子邮件向《财富》杂志发表的声明是对所发生事件的最清晰的陈述。 对于测序也异常坦诚。

她说，这次发布“验证了需求，但也向我们表明，我们需要降低完成人工智能任务的成本，以支持广泛的推广”。

然后就决定了。 “我们决定在重建架构、降低单位成本和强化业务模式的同时放慢推出速度，而不是在基础经济准备就绪之前广泛推出产品。”

她表示，自 4 月份 Canva AI 2.0 推出以来，每项任务的成本已下降了近 90%。 用户创建的设计数量是原来的三倍，因此节省的费用并未达到百分比所建议的水平。

到底是什么打破了

Pitchbook 负责 SaaS 和人工智能的高级研究分析师德里克·埃尔南德斯 (Derek Hernandez) 向《财富》杂志提供了结构版本。 软件的经济性是受害者。

“人工智能使 SaaS 不再是零边际成本解决方案，到目前为止，这确实是我所说的许多软件的秘密武器，”他说。

他的类比是有用的部分。 制造福特 F-150 是训练，汽油和机械师是推理，“因为这就是使用该产品的目的”。

过去，为多一个用户提供一种设计工具几乎不需要任何成本。 现在，每张人工智能辅助图像都附有计算账单。

相隔五天

埃尔南德斯还提供了将其连接到上市市场的线路。 “Canva 和 Figma 都在相隔大约五天的时间里碰上了同一堵墙，但他们在不同的地方引用了它，”他说。

Figma 增长了 48% 并上调了预期，其股价因利润率下跌了 16%。

第二季度其自由现金流利润率从第一季度的 27% 降至 14%。 它将第三季度的增长率从 48% 下调至 36%。

一家公司是上市公司，一天之内就重新定价。 另一个是私有的，由股东重新定价。 同一堵墙。

同一张账单正在到达其他地方

大买家也纷纷入手。 亚马逊负责克劳德的工作，在失败之前超出了预算 860%。

反应正在趋同。 微软对内部人工智能的使用设定了支出限制。

安永构建了一个人工智能路由器，将任务发送到更便宜的模型，而不是默认到前沿。 这与帕金斯描述的重建很接近。

Scale Venture Partners 的 Rory O’Driscoll 在 20VC 播客上提出了时机的争论。 他说：“将会有很多人在 26 和 27 日买单，而在 23 和 24 日会有一定程度的犹豫。”

为什么 Canva 不能袖手旁观

人工智能不是这里的一个功能，而是扩展计划。 Canva 一直在将设计推向企业工作流程，添加了包括 Canva Code 在内的工具。

帕金斯在 2023 年向《财富》杂志表示，人工智能市场过于分散。 此后的策略是将这些部分整合到一个平台中。

这就是《财富》杂志为整个行业提出的困境。 公司不能错过人工智能的繁荣，拥抱它可能会破坏他们所保护的经济。

欧洲也有一家处于同样前提下的进入者，但目前还没有可比的利润率历史记录。 Lovable 的收入达到 5 亿美元，拥有 146 名员工。

上市是刹车的原因

Canva 在一次员工股票出售中估值为 420 亿美元，预计将于 2026 年上市。 埃尔南德斯现在建议明年。

他认为经济放缓是面向投资者的。 “我确信他们正在努力保护自己的盈利能力，特别是如果他们想向公共投资者寻求帮助的话，”他说。

利润修复后的 20% 增长与成本问题下的 30% 增长是不同的。 Figma 建议公开市场立即惩罚第二个。

什么可以解决它

三件事，第一是下一份收入印刷品。 Canva 的目标是 20% 左右，这一点是否成立表明成本问题是得到解决还是推迟。

第二个是90%的说法。 每项任务的成本大幅下降，而使用量却增加了三倍，这是可以在几个季度内进行测试的。

第三是还有谁因此而被降分。 Hernandez 称 Canva 和 Figma 是迄今为止最大的信号，这意味着更多信号即将到来。
